metadata.title: Data Density Pass 17 -- Day 1 Late Afternoon (Ticks 62-100)
metadata.description: Individual regiment records for the rout through Gettysburg town and the critical consolidation on Cemetery Hill. XI Corps retreat, Rodes and Early pursuing, the key stand by Buford and Howard on Cemetery Hill, the arrival of Hancock to stabilize the Union position, and Gordon's brief occupation of Gettysburg streets. The moment when Ewell fails to take Cemetery Hill.

placements.notes: Gordon's brigade chasing XI Corps through Gettysburg town -- Gordon urges Ewell to press the attack
17th Connecticut retreating through Gettysburg -- will reform on East Cemetery Hill
Rodes's remaining brigades pursuing I Corps remnants toward Seminary Ridge
16th Maine sacrifice stand on Seminary Ridge -- ordered to hold as all others retreat to buy time
143rd PA retreating -- Seminary Ridge untenable
Wadsworth's division rallied on Cemetery Hill -- forming the nucleus of the Union defense
Robinson's division reforming on Cemetery Hill -- badly cut up but still in hand
Barlow's XI Corps division reforming -- 50% casualties from Barlows Knoll
Schurz's division on Cemetery Hill
Gordon halted -- Ewell will not order the advance on Cemetery Hill. Gordon is furious.
Gordon's brigade halted in Gettysburg streets. The moment passes.
Hancock arriving from Taneytown on horseback -- sent by Meade to stabilize the position
Hancock takes command of Cemetery Hill by Meade's orders. He places the I and XI Corps.
Buford's cavalry screening the Union left -- fighting delaying action on Chambersburg Pike
Pender's division on Seminary Ridge -- Hill considers attacking but receives no orders from Lee
Iron Brigade survivors on Cemetery Hill -- down from 1800 this morning
Schimmelfennig's XI Corps division -- Schimmelfennig hiding in a pigsty in town
XII Corps arriving on Baltimore Pike -- Slocum will defend Culp's Hill
XII Corps deploying on Culp's Hill -- Slocum and Williams anchoring the right
Early's division on the northern edge of Gettysburg -- Ewell's decision not to attack crystallizing
Rodes's division -- waiting for the order that never comes
